Habit formation is the process of developing a routine that makes a specific behavior automatic. It starts with a cue, routine, and reward. The cue is a trigger that signals to your brain that it's time to do the habit. The routine is the action that you take in response to the cue. The reward is the positive outcome that you receive when you complete the routine. Over time, the brain starts to associate the cue with the routine and rewards, so that the routine becomes automatic. This makes it easier to perform the habit without having to think about it. 

Small routines can compound over time and create a powerful habit. When you start with a small routine, it becomes easier to maintain. As the habit becomes automatic, you can focus on other important tasks without getting distracted by the habit. This can lead to increased productivity and efficiency. Over time, small routines can compound and create a powerful habit that has a positive impact on your life.
